This blog is my attempt to write publicly about the things I spend my days thinking about: population genetics, statistical genomics, and the challenge of understanding human genetic diversity in all its complexity.

## What you'll find here

A few times a month I plan to post:

- **Methods tutorials** — walkthroughs of tools like PLINK, ADMIXTURE, VCFtools, and SMC++ with real code and real output. The kind of post I wish had existed when I was learning.
- **Paper commentary** — my read on new preprints and publications in the pop-gen space. What's interesting, what's novel, what I'm skeptical about.
- **Analysis walkthroughs** — worked examples using R, usually including the actual code blocks so you can follow along or adapt them to your own data.
- **Opinion pieces** — occasional longer-form thoughts on where the field is heading, equity in genomics research, and what it means to do population genetics responsibly with underrepresented groups.

## Who this is for

Broadly: scientists and students who are curious about population genetics but aren't necessarily specialists. I'll assume you're comfortable with basic genetics and statistics, but I'll try to explain the population-genetics-specific concepts rather than assuming everyone has read Hartl & Clark cover to cover.

## A note on the research

My work focuses mainly on Indigenous Australian and Southeast Asian populations — groups that are genomically understudied relative to their diversity and their disease burden. A lot of standard pop-gen methods were developed and validated on European-ancestry cohorts. Understanding where they work, where they break down, and how to do better is one of the central questions I keep coming back to.

More soon.
